TL;DR: Dark Souls 3 will have at its core the theme of The age of Ancients vs the Cycle of Fire and Dark the world is stuck in.

Dark souls created a beautiful lore to explore. It told the story of THE most important event in the world of Dark Souls...that being the advent of Fire (capital "F")

Before Fire the world was unformed and in stasis, grey crags arch trees and Everlasting Dragons filled the world. Fire brought Disparity in the form of heat and cold, life and death and Light and Dark (again proper nouns for these last two) The stasis of the everlasting unformed world was broken...and then something happened..."from the Dark They came and found the Souls of Lords in the flame."

Gwyn, Nito, the Witch of Izalith, and the Furtive Pygmy each found souls.

With these souls they had power to war with the dragons and destroy the archtrees and they found themselves in control of the new world at the dawn of the age of fire.

But with Disparity comes Cycles. The age of Fire waned as the flame died and only embers remain as the dark sign begins to be seen in humans. The undead curse runs rampant and becomes such a problem that the undead are corralled in the Undead Asylum and possibly other places. It is here that they await the end of the world...whatever that entails.

From here an undead goes to Lordran and learns that he can prolong the age of fire by linking the flame as Gwyn had done...or can usher in an age of dark by letting the fire die and this age is also known as the age of man.

There are some details that are worth mentioning about souls and humanity. Souls are the source of all life...all living things posses souls. Humanity on the other hand is unique to humans...it defines them. Humanity is a physical thing and is described as a sprite. Manus's soul is a lump of gentle humanity. The fire keepers skin seethes with writhing infinite humanity just under the surface. The point is Humanity sprites seem to be fragments of the original souls that the Furtive Pygmy found...the Dark Soul. It was unique and its power grows as the fire subsides.

Gwyn feared this and humans as they were associated with humanity.

Thus Dark souls 2 begins...dark souls 2 introduces us to only 2 important lore points as far as I know. 1) The choice you make at the end of Dark Souls makes no difference because the age of Fire and Man/Dark are locked in an Ebb and Flow. At some point the flame will be kindled and the age of Fire renewed...it will then fade and then be kindled again. 2) Insight into the nature of souls...this really isn't taught to us through Aldia and his experiments and studies into the nature of the soul but it is taught through the reincarnation of the Souls of Lords as seen in The lost sinner-this is the Witch's soul, Dear Freja-this is Seath's soul, The Old Iron King has (I suspect) The remnant of Gwyn's soul. (what was left after he gave shards to the 4 kings and Seath), and The Rotten has Nito's soul. What does this teach us? That the souls are immortal and innately hold their characteristics.

My theory is that the souls fill empty husks, or vessels and impart life (and death)..."They came from the dark and in the flame found the souls of lords" who were THEY? I think they were empty vessels that the souls filled...thus CREATING the Gods from the 3 souls of light and creating the first man from the Dark Soul. These souls...not their vessels are immortal

The larger story of Dark Souls I think is the conflict between these SOULS (the givers of all life..), and the World that came before...or the Everlasting Dragons. Perhaps it is the Primordial Serpents that seek to maintain the cycle of Fire and Dark and not return to the Stasis of the Age of Ancients. Kaanthe and Frampt seem to be at odds but they are liars out only to sustain the cycle.

What is the point of all this rambling? I think that Dark Souls 3 will deal with the larger theme of Stasis and Disparity...not Fire and Dark. Fire and Dark is a cycle in a world of disparity...to end the cycle is to end the Disparity and return to the world as it was in the age of ancients...no death...no life...just grey crags and arch trees...and maybe a stone dragon or two. THIS is the End of the World that the undead await in the Asylum. A return to stasis...and end to the cycle of life and death.
